THE_DEFECT_THIS_COMPENSATES_FOR.what_it_does: Validates the source NPZ by PATH and SIZE, confirms the receipt CARRIES a sha256, then assigns receipt['_verified_input_sha256'] = source['sha256'] -- copying the receipt's own claim into a field named `_verified_`. The file is never hashed.
THE_DEFECT_THIS_COMPENSATES_FOR.the_contrast_is_INSIDE_THE_SAME_FUNCTION: At :99 the TARGET is genuinely hashed -- `target_sha = sha256_file(target_npy)` -- then compared to its receipt and its size checked. So the same function hashes one artifact and not the other, and writes both into `_verified_*` fields. `sha256_file` is defined at :36 and already called at :99, so the tool was in hand.
THE_DEFECT_THIS_COMPENSATES_FOR.the_asymmetry_is_the_tell: `_verified_target_sha256 = target_sha` (COMPUTED) sits directly beside `_verified_input_sha256 = source['sha256']` (COPIED). Identical prefix, opposite epistemic status.
THE_DEFECT_THIS_COMPENSATES_FOR.why_the_NAME_is_worse_than_the_omission: A missing check is a gap a reader can look for. A field called `_verified_input_sha256` holding an unverified value actively answers the question a reader would ask -- it is a relayed claim wearing the name of a measurement. Contrast train_fullevent_nominal.py:277, which DOES hash and whose comment names the same-size-substitution case explicitly.
THE_DEFECT_THIS_COMPENSATES_FOR.found_by: the mediator lane; verified here by reading the source rather than accepting the report
THE_DEFECT_THIS_COMPENSATES_FOR.severity_in_practice: The size check at :109 would catch truncation or a differently-sized substitution. What it cannot catch is a same-size different-content file, which is precisely the case nominal.py:277's comment calls out.
